sections.h2: The bay, flood zones and your sale
sections.html:
Panama City sits on St. Andrews Bay in the Florida Panhandle. The bay wraps much of the city and shelters the harbor of the Port of Panama City complex. Moisture and salt air shape what buyers inspect first: roofs, window seals, siding and anything near the water.

Bay County tells residents to look up their address on its evacuation zone map, and the zones may differ from what people assume. The county's floodplain ordinance was updated to federally required standards with new flood maps, and the county keeps a copy of the updated flood zones in its map gallery. Ask which map your parcel sits on before you describe flood risk to a buyer. A seller who knows the evacuation zone and the flood map status of the lot can answer the questions insurers and buyers raise early.

The water is the draw. The city has public boat ramps at St. Andrews Marina, Downtown Marina, Carl Gray Park, Snug Harbor and Bob George Park, and two city marinas on the Intracoastal Waterway take vessels up to 130 feet. Downtown holds the Center for the Arts, and St. Andrews, Downtown and Millville are tied together by a mural trail.

Give your distance to any of these in plain miles, since a buyer will check it on a map. Bay County also funds road and utility projects through a half-cent surtax and posts an interactive project map, so you can point a buyer there instead of guessing which streets are slated for work.

Pull every permit, final inspection and certificate for work done on the house. The city requires a permit before a project starts, including reroofing, decks, carports, sheds, remodels and changes to electrical, plumbing, mechanical, structural, irrigation or insulation systems.

The duty to confirm permits rests on the owner or the owner's authorized agent. A permit goes invalid if work does not begin within 6 months of issuance or stops for 6 months after it starts, and an extension must be requested in writing with a fee. Work has to stay exposed for inspection until approved.

The city issues a certificate of occupancy for a structure and a certificate of completion where occupancy does not apply, such as a reroof or system alteration. Building Services is at 501 Harrison Ave., phone 850-872-3025. Some projects need approval from other agencies too, such as the Florida Department of Environmental Protection.

sections.h2: Bay County tax dates and discounts
sections.html:
Notices are normally mailed on or before November 1 with a due date of March 31, and unpaid taxes turn delinquent April 1. Discounts shrink month by month.

Early-payment discounts on Bay County real estate taxes
Month paidDiscount
November4%
December3%
January2%
February1%

Non-ad valorem charges for paving, stormwater and solid waste ride on the same bill and also become delinquent April 1. Changes to a name, address, location or assessed value go through the property appraiser. If an escrow servicer pays your bill, ask it to request the original notice so you get a copy.

sections.h2: Paying or asking questions in person
sections.html:
The Bay County Tax Collector runs offices in Panama City at 850 W. 11th St., Panama City Beach at 10520 Hutchison Blvd., Lynn Haven at 700 Florida Ave. and Callaway at 805 S. Tyndall Pkwy. Renewal kiosks sit inside the Publix stores on W. 23rd St. and on Panama City Beach Parkway.

  • Bring the tax notice or the property address. Only Bay County property tax is taken at these counters.
  • Delinquent payments must be made with certified funds: cash, cashier's check, money order or card.
  • Appointments can be booked online for each office.

Homestead does not stay with the house. The exemption belongs to the resident owner, and a sale lifts the capped assessment back to full market-based value at the start of the next year, so a buyer can open with a bigger bill than yours.

A permanent home can lose up to $50,000 of taxable value, with school taxes touched only by the first $25,000. The Bay County property appraiser takes applications until March 1. If you are moving within Florida, portability can carry your capped savings to the next house, provided you set up that homestead inside three years.

Voters considered Amendment 3, a constitutional change on the November 3, 2026 ballot that would raise the non-school homestead exemption if 60 percent approved. Ask the property appraiser what the outcome means for your parcel.

Bay County also requires registration, reporting and inspection for vacation rentals in the unincorporated areas. That is worth knowing if your house has been used for short stays and the new owner wants to continue.

sections.h2: Deed charges at a Bay County closing
sections.html:
Florida's deed tax is seventy cents per hundred dollars of price, and all parties to the deed stay liable for it. The clerk takes it at recording.

Recording fees open at five dollars for page one and four dollars for every later page, then add a trust fund charge and a technology charge per page. A mortgage the buyer assumes counts toward the consideration, so the closing agent adds it to the total.

sections.h2: Inherited, rented or behind on taxes
sections.html:
Each case has its own clock. Florida offers a shortcut for modest estates and a short written demand for unpaid rent, so ask a lawyer which route fits.

If tax stays unpaid, the county sells a certificate against the parcel and an investor can eventually seek a tax deed, which is why a payoff matters. Collect the payoff letter, the lease or the court file before you weigh an offer.

After you accept an offer, the title company searches for liens, unpaid taxes and open permits, and the closing agent prepares the deed and the settlement statement. A cash buyer skips the lender's appraisal and underwriting, which removes the longest wait. Bring a photo ID, the payoff letter if a mortgage remains, and permit papers for any roof or system work. Settle utility accounts for closing day, and leave keys and any warranties for the buyer. Ask the closing agent how and when your proceeds will arrive.

If the house has storm or water history, gather repair invoices, insurance claim papers and any elevation or flood zone documents, since a buyer's insurer will want them before binding coverage. Sellers with a tenant should add the lease and rent ledger. When the file is complete, the title company can often clear the house faster, and a cash buyer can set a closing date that fits your move.

faqs.q: How is Panama City located on the bay?
faqs.a: Panama City sits on St. Andrews Bay in the Florida Panhandle, and the bay wraps much of the city. Look up your address on the county evacuation zone map and check your flood zone before you list.

faqs.q: When are Bay County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Notices go out on or before November 1 with a due date of March 31. Taxes unpaid after that become delinquent on April 1.

faqs.q: Which permits should I check before selling in Panama City?
faqs.a: Check permits for roofs, decks, sheds, remodels and electrical, plumbing, mechanical and structural work, plus any certificate of occupancy or completion. Call Building Services at 850-872-3025.

faqs.q: Does the Bay County Tax Collector have an office on Panama City Beach?
faqs.a: Yes. It has an office at 10520 Hutchison Blvd., Panama City Beach, along with offices in Panama City, Lynn Haven and Callaway.

faqs.q: Can homestead carry over to a house I buy next?
faqs.a: Partly. Portability can transfer the Save Our Homes difference to a new Florida homestead if you establish it within three years, and you file for it with the new county's property appraiser.
